scope: Targeted, non-systematic comparison of seven selected prior works against the next proposed Catholic institutional evidence-representation evaluation.
methods: Search for direct Catholic-source retrieval and doctrine evaluations; faith-sensitive pastoral triage; religion and canon-law studies; religious organizational governance; citation-support assessment; human oversight-to-control documentary frameworks.
Check issuer or publisher pages and accessible abstracts or full HTML for title, evidence type, and reported method.
Translate overlaps into falsifiable discriminating tests without treating non-exhaustive search as proof of priority.
Preserve citations, review-depth and unknowns; propose no new confirmatory cases or completed expert judgments.

papers.citation: von Däniken, P.; Cieliebak, M.; Deriu, J. C4: A Multilingual Benchmark for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Based on the Catechism of the Catholic Church and Its Compendium. LREC 2026.
papers.empirical_scope: Multilingual Catholic Catechism and Compendium RAG datasets with collection scripts and baseline retrieval/generation results.
papers.overlap: Direct precedent for Catholic grounded retrieval and citation-aligned answer evaluation.
papers.outside_scope: No reported comparison in its abstract of identical-evidence human reviewers applying institutional control-operation records.
papers.implication: Do not claim first Catholic RAG evaluation. Reuse its principle of paragraph-aligned source references, with rights and version controls.

papers.citation: Owen, J. Detecting doctrinal flattening in AI generated responses. AI and Ethics 6, 178 (2026).
papers.empirical_scope: 576 source-derived atomic doctrinal claims from 11 Christian traditions, compared with two model outputs using structured text matching and doctrinal heuristics.
papers.overlap: Direct precedent for doctrinal-claim support, omission and tradition-specific theological differences.
papers.outside_scope: Human institutional reviewer intervention and effectiveness of documentary control records are not its primary dependent variables.
papers.implication: Account for omission and qualifiers, not only contradictions; distinguish automated reference labels from independently verified theology.

papers.citation: Chao, A. When AI Is Your Pastor: A Benchmark for Theological Triage and Pastoral Guidance in Large Language Models. FMG-Bench (2026 preprint).
papers.empirical_scope: 120 Christian pastoral/doctrinal scenarios, 14 models and 8,792 scored responses across guided and unguided instruction conditions; measures escalation appropriateness.
papers.overlap: Direct precedent for pastoral redirection, authority-sensitive triage and evaluation of prompts and instructions.
papers.outside_scope: Proposed referrals as model text do not measure a completed human referral, acknowledged receipt or institutional remedy.
papers.implication: Test delivered/acknowledged human intervention only when a real workflow can be observed; do not mistake written advice for executed safeguards.

papers.citation: Falletti, E.; Trovato, G. Diritto canonico e machine learning: il caso del robot SanTO. Stato, Chiese e pluralismo confessionale 11 (2025).
papers.empirical_scope: Legal and canonical analysis of an AI-enabled Catholic prayer robot that may consult a local database or a large language model.
papers.overlap: Direct Catholic AI and canon-law authority precedent.
papers.outside_scope: Abstract does not describe a randomized, reviewer-outcome comparator on source-control evidence representations.
papers.implication: Catholic-domain and canon-law framing alone cannot establish novelty; qualified application must be reviewed.

papers.citation: Cheong, P.; Liu, L.; Nord, I. et al. Artificial intelligence, religion, and society: ethical leadership and the shaping of value-based adaptive governance. AI and Ethics 6, 561 (2026).
papers.empirical_scope: Qualitative comparative cases involving 66 Christian religious leaders in the United States, Germany and Switzerland; identifies normative, collaborative and experimentative adaptive governance.
papers.overlap: Empirical precedent for Christian institutional AI adoption, authority and shared responsibility.
papers.outside_scope: Does not experimentally compare reviewer error or review time between uncertainty-aware checklist and CEC evidence record presentations.
papers.implication: Do not claim religious institutional AI governance has not been studied. Use institutional stakeholder and responsibility distinctions.

papers.citation: An automated framework for assessing how well LLMs cite relevant medical references (SourceCheckup). Nature Communications (2025).
papers.empirical_scope: 800 medical questions and 58,000 statement-source pairs across seven models; compares source support with independent physician assessments.
papers.overlap: Very strong direct precedent for automated claim-to-citation support evaluation validated against qualified humans.
papers.outside_scope: Medical source faithfulness does not directly measure church-specific authority, real intervention and post-error propagation within a bounded institutional control opportunity.
papers.implication: Claim-level citation support is not novel. A reviewer-outcome comparison must show an added result beyond SourceCheckup, controlling for source completeness.

papers.citation: Hardy, K. From human oversight to effective control: A comparative documentary framework for high-impact AI systems. Digital Policy (online first 2026).
papers.empirical_scope: Eight prescriptive instruments, 19 public cases and 41 oversight/control evidence statements; six functions Observe, Detect, Interpret, Challenge and Decide, Intervene, Recover and Learn.
papers.overlap: Very strong conceptual and documentary precedent for the claim that nominal human oversight is not evidence of practical control.
papers.outside_scope: Author explicitly notes purposive/public-record and single-researcher limits and need for prospective independent validation; no documented randomized same-evidence Catholic reviewer comparison in accessible abstract.
papers.implication: Compare constructs and reuse appropriate terminology with attribution, then test prospective independent reviewer outcomes rather than asserting first evidence-to-control framework.

open_novelty_claim: No first-of-kind claim established. The candidate distinctive test is a prospective, independently rated, same-evidence comparison of a strong uncertainty-aware checklist and CEC-style event/source/authority/intervention records in a Catholic institutional context.

planned_study.study_unit: One documentable AI-assisted institutional control opportunity, identified by event, relevant source, authority boundary, human opportunity and time window.
planned_study.primary_question: Does a CEC-style evidence-to-control record reduce unsupported categorical conclusions by independently qualified reviewers compared with a strong uncertainty-aware checklist when all reviewers receive the same source packet?
planned_study.design: Two presentation arms, using exactly the same frozen source passages and event/control evidence. Randomly allocate different reviewers to each case/arm; no reviewer sees a case in both formats before their initial judgment. Balance case difficulty and expertise. Outcome adjudicators blind to arm where possible.
planned_study.baseline: A competent narrative+checklist explicitly requiring source identity, semantic support, applicability, decision authority, intervention evidence and unresolved/abstain states, with citations and the same evidence as treatment.
planned_study.treatment: A CEC-structured representation separating source assertions, claim support, institutional applicability, delegated authority, notice/opportunity, intervention, downstream effect and unresolved evidence, with traceable source IDs. No privileged facts or additional tools.
planned_study.primary_candidate: Unsupported categorical verdict count divided by all evaluable case decisions; case eligibility and adjudication definitions must be prespecified.
planned_study.anti_abstention_gate: Simultaneously measure correct determinate conclusions on independently decidable cases; abstaining on all records must not be counted as success.
secondary_candidates: Correct supported conclusion retention on adjudicated determinate cases
Time per decision and record inspection effort
False claims that a referral, override or remedy reached its target
Reviewer explanation/source trace quality and disagreement documentation
candidate_strata: Source support: exact reference correct, mismatched or semantically insufficient
Institutional authority: document sound, but norm's applicability or speaker authority uncertain
Operational control: approval or intervention attempted, propagation/receipt/effect unobserved
must_freeze_before_run: Study owner approves target population, outcomes and estimator
Independent reviewer qualifications/AI exposure and consent approved
Rights-cleared new case packets independent of PQA-01 through 06 and authored 24-case development fixtures
Primary endpoint numerator and denominator, exclusions, abstentions and missingness defined
Blinding and randomization/carryover avoidance procedure set
Sample-size justification and stopping/budget rules recorded
Competent canonical and theological advice for normative reference labels
Program AI disclosure and research ethics/institutional permission assessed
falsification_conditions: Checklist matches CEC accuracy with less review burden
CEC induces false certainty or hides evidence gaps
Any observed benefit disappears with reviewer expertise or matched source completeness
Independent reviewer agreement is too low to establish determinate outcomes
Records cannot show receipt or effect of purported human intervention

conclusions.statement: Catholic retrieval and doctrinal-response evaluation have direct published precedents; categorical first-in-field claims fail.
SourceCheckup includes independent clinician corroboration of claim-source support; human expert calibration is established in an adjacent high-stakes domain.
Hardy's O2C provides an explicit control-evidence framework; effective oversight distinct from named humans is already studied.
CEC's 24-case citation engineering comparison recorded no admission advantage of a structured gate over a fair simple checklist.
Matched-evidence independent human reviewers might benefit from preserving source/authority/intervention/receipt as distinct evidence questions; efficacy is untested.

screening_limits: Targeted selection by topic, not a systematic literature review, PRISMA search, citation network survey or comprehensive novelty determination.
Different sources reviewed at different depth; some publisher abstracts only and no independent full-PDF reading for all papers.
Published benchmarks differ in populations, tasks, denominators and rating methods; their reported metrics must not be pooled or imported as Catholic pilot performance.
SourceCheckup's physician agreement and Hardy's documentary coding do not establish the CEC intervention effect.
No independently qualified Catholic reviewers, case adjudications or consent were obtained through this desk review.
